title: Day 80 · Week 11, Day 3 — Parents: her mood — the depression that peaks before the birth, the one in four who is anxious, the ten questions on the clipboard, and what a partner can see that a form can't
summary: Depression and anxiety during pregnancy, not after it. Your baby is about 4.5 cm and under 10 g, kidneys making urine and the placenta finishing its hormone handover. The numbers: depression in 7.4% of women in the first trimester and about 12–13% in the second and third (Bennett 2004, 21 studies, 19,284 women); in ALSPAC 13.5% were above the depression threshold at 32 weeks of pregnancy versus 9.1% at 8 weeks postpartum (Evans 2001); anxiety symptoms in 18.2%, 19.1% and 24.6% by trimester and an anxiety disorder in 15.2% (Dennis 2017, 102 studies, 221,974 women); antenatal anxiety roughly tripling the odds of postnatal depression (Heron 2004, 8,323 women). The risk factors that survive adjustment — life stress, low social support and domestic violence (Lancaster 2010). Why it matters: preterm birth RR 1.39 and low birth weight RR 1.49 where depression is categorised, with the confounding caveat (Grote 2010), and mental health conditions as the leading underlying cause of US pregnancy-related deaths (about 23%, CDC MMRC 2017–2019). The screening: ACOG CPG 4 (2023) — screen at the first visit, later in pregnancy and postpartum; the 10-item Edinburgh scale and its accuracy (sensitivity 81%, specificity 88% at ≥11; Levis 2020, 15,557 women); the Whooley questions and the 'would you like help?' question (specificity 94%, Arroll 2005). Treatment: counselling cuts onset by 39% in women at risk (USPSTF 2019, grade B); SSRIs and heart defects — RR 1.06 once depression is accounted for (Huybrechts 2014, 949,504 pregnancies). The partner's part: support and conflict in the Pilkington meta-analysis, the 29-woman Misri trial, the signs worth noticing over two weeks, how to raise it, and the situations that mean calling the same day — with the 988 Lifeline and the National Maternal Mental Health Hotline.
action: Add a 'Mood' section to the pregnancy file with two lines: any history of depression or anxiety in either of you, and what helped; and the two numbers — 988 Suicide and Crisis Lifeline (call or text 988) and the National Maternal Mental Health Hotline, 1-833-TLC-MAMA (1-833-852-6262). Save the hotline in your phone.
